facts.statement: Eodromaeus is an extinct genus of basal theropod dinosaurs that lived in the Late Triassic of Argentina.
facts.quote: Eodromaeus (meaning "dawn runner") is an extinct genus of probable basal theropod dinosaurs from the Late Triassic of Argentina.

facts.statement: Eodromaeus lived approximately 230 million years ago in the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic within the Ischigualasto Formation in northwestern Argentina.
facts.quote: Like many other of the earliest-known dinosaurs, it hails from the Carnian-age (~230 Ma) Ischigualasto Formation, within the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin of northwestern Argentina.

facts.statement: Fossils of Eodromaeus were first discovered in 1996 by paleontologist Ricardo N. Martinez and volunteer Jim Murphy.
facts.quote: Fossils from Eodromaeus were first discovered in 1996 by Argentinean paleontologist Ricardo N. Martinez and Earthwatch volunteer Jim Murphy

facts.statement: The genus Eodromaeus and its type species E. murphi were named in 2011 by a team including Ricardo N. Martinez and Paul C. Sereno.
facts.quote: Eodromaeus was named by Ricardo N. Martínez, Paul C. Sereno, Oscar A. Alcober, Carina E. Colombi, Paul R. Renne, Isabel P. Montañez and Brian S. Currie in 2011 and the type species is Eodromaeus murphi.

facts.statement: The name Eodromaeus combines the Greek words for 'dawn' and 'runner'.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Greek words Eos ("Dawn", "Early") and Dromaeus ("Runner").

facts.statement: The species name 'murphi' honors Jim Murphy, who worked near the fossil discovery site.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Jim Murphy, who used to work the area nearby where the fossils were found.

facts.statement: Eodromaeus was a relatively small dinosaur, typical of most Carnian dinosaurs except herrerasaurids.
facts.quote: Eodromaeus was a relatively small dinosaur, like most Carnian dinosaurs apart from herrerasaurids.

facts.statement: Eodromaeus reached a total length of about 1.2 meters and weighed between 4.5 and 6.8 kilograms.
facts.quote: A press release estimated that its total length reach about 1.2 m from nose to tail, with a weight of about 4.5 to 6.8 kg.

facts.statement: Paul Sereno estimated that Eodromaeus could run at speeds of about 32 kilometers per hour.
facts.quote: Paul Sereno has estimated that it could run about 32 km per hour (20 miles per hour).

facts.statement: Eodromaeus had a low, rectangular skull approximately 12 centimeters long.
facts.quote: The skull was low and rectangular, about 12 cm in length.

facts.statement: The skull of Eodromaeus featured an expansive antorbital fenestra edged below by a sharp ridge.
facts.quote: It had an expansive antorbital fenestra edged from below by a sharp ridge.

facts.statement: Eodromaeus possessed fifteen knife-shaped teeth in its cranium, with the longest ones located in the front half of the upper jaw.
facts.quote: The cranium had a relatively low number of knife-shaped teeth (fifteen in total) which were longest in the front half of the maxilla.

facts.statement: A row of tiny teeth was present on the pterygoid bone of the palate in Eodromaeus.
facts.quote: There was also a row of tiny teeth on the pterygoid bone of the palate.

facts.statement: The fourth and fifth fingers of Eodromaeus were very thin and short.
facts.quote: In contrast, the fourth and fifth fingers were very thin and short.

facts.statement: When first described in 2011, Eodromaeus was considered the earliest member of the Theropoda.
facts.quote: When originally described in 2011, Eodromaeus was regarded as the earliest member of Theropoda.

facts.statement: A later study by Baron et al. (2017) placed Eodromaeus as a basal herrerasaurian and moved the family Herrerasauridae outside of Dinosauria.
facts.quote: A subsequent response to that critique, by Baron et al. (2017), placed Eodromaeus as a basal herrerasaurian and simultaneously shifted the entire family Herrerasauridae outside of Dinosauria.

facts.statement: All known specimens of Eodromaeus lived within the humid Scaphonyx-Exaeretodon-Herrerasaurus biozone in the Ischigualasto Formation.
facts.quote: Every Eodromaeus specimen lived within the humid Scaphonyx-Exaeretodon-Herrerasaurus biozone, which occupies the first half of the Ischigualasto Formation.

facts.statement: Eodromaeus is classified within the order Saurischia.
facts.quote: ordo: Saurischia

facts.statement: Eodromaeus belongs to the suborder Theropoda.
facts.quote: subordo: Theropoda

facts.statement: Eodromaeus was a relatively small dinosaur with a total length of approximately 1.2 meters and a weight of about 5 kilograms.
facts.quote: Eodromaeus era un dinosaurio relativamente pequeño, con una longitud total de aproximadamente 1,2 metros desde la nariz hasta la cola, y un peso de aproximadamente 5 kilogramos.

facts.statement: While the exact speed is unknown, it has been suggested that Eodromaeus could run at about 30 kilometers per hour.
facts.quote: No se sabe qué tan rápido podría correr Eodromaeus , pero se ha sugerido a unos 30 kilómetros por hora.

facts.statement: Eodromaeus was a basal carnivorous theropod with forelimbs much shorter than its hindlimbs, ending in hands with five digits.
facts.quote: Es un terópodo carnívoro basal con las extremidades anteriores eran mucho más cortas que las extremidades posteriores, terminando en manos con 5 dígitos.

facts.statement: The specific name murphi honors James Murphy.
facts.quote: El nombre específico murphi es en honor a James Murphy.

facts.statement: This basal theropod lived during the Late Triassic, specifically the mid-Carnian stage, approximately 231.4 to 229 million years ago in what is now Argentina.
facts.quote: Se trata de un terópodo basal, que vivió durante el periodo Triásico Superior a mediados de la época del Carniense, hace aproximadamente 231.4-229 millones de años en lo que hoy es Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus was named in 2011 by Ricardo N. Martínez, Paul C. Sereno, Oscar A. Alcober, Carina E. Colombi, Paul R. Renne, Isabel P. Montañez, and Brian S. Currie, with the type species being Eodromaeus murphi.
facts.quote: Eodromaeus fue nombrado por Ricardo N. Martínez, Paul C. Sereno, Oscar A. Alcober, Carina E. Colombi, Paul R. Renne, Isabel P. Montañez y Brian S. Currie en 2011 y la especie tipo es Eodromaeus murphi.

facts.statement: Eodromaeus is considered one of the earliest members of Theropoda, the group that includes carnivorous dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Eodromaeus es considerado como uno de los primeros miembros de Theropoda, el grupo que incluye a los dinosaurios carnívoros.

facts.statement: The discovery of Eodromaeus led some researchers to believe that Eoraptor, generally considered a theropod, likely represented one of the most basal sauropodomorphs, the group that includes animals like Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de Eodromaeus llevó a algunos a creer que Eoraptor, generalmente considerado como un terópodo, probablemente representaba uno de los sauropodomorfos más basales, el grupo que incluye animales como Apatosaurus.

facts.statement: This hypothesis has been questioned since then, with Bergman and Sues claiming Eoraptor as a theropod, like Eodromaeus.
facts.quote: Esto ha sido cuestionado desde entonces, con Bergman y Sues reclamando a Eoraptor como un terópodo, como Eodromaeus.

facts.statement: The parent group of Eodromaeus is Saurischia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Saurischia

facts.statement: The time range for Eodromaeus is the Carnian stage, from 237 to 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)
